title: NVIDIA Just Changed AI Data Centers FOREVER!!
creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
summary: Jose Najarro covers Nvidia's GTC Berlin announcements and earnings from Lam Research, Texas Instruments and Meta. The headline is Nvidia's DSX pods: shipping containers pre-built with Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, power and cooling, which he says cut AI-factory build time from about six months to as little as 14 days, reducing lender and execution risk and reinforcing Nvidia as the only supplier offering this. On Lam Research (captions say 'Lamb Research'), down about 7.4% after a narrow beat, he says he is not a shareholder but would not fear the sell-off, noting wafer-fab equipment spending above $200 billion expected in 2027. On Texas Instruments, Q3 revenue was $6.06 billion, up 28% year over year, with data-centre revenue up about 95%, industrial up over 40% and automotive up mid-teens. On Meta, he calls the report extremely bullish for the AI cycle: revenue up 26%, Q4 guidance of $73–76 billion, the capex lower bound raised to $135 billion, strong Muse adoption, and a new Class C share he reads as preparation for large capex fundraising. Calls: NVDA — BUY reiterated, very bullish, no price stated; LRCX — UNCERTAIN (first tracked, positive coverage only); TXN — UNCERTAIN (first tracked, positive coverage only); META — UNCERTAIN (bullish read-through only, no explicit buy).

calls.thesis: Very, very bullish reiterated: the new DSX pods (captions render them 'DSX') — pre-built shipping-container AI factories with Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, power and cooling built in — cut AI-factory production from ~6 months to as little as 14 days, removing execution and lender risk and making Nvidia the only supplier doing this right now; he calls it a massive win that lets Nvidia scale and sell more. Other GTC Berlin items (agent safety, robotics, Vera vs Blackwell) were mostly repeats for channel followers.
calls.price_at_call: Up ~2.5% on the day, down ~1.2% after hours; no share price stated
